small_guidance:
- Swap the inner loop order so IC is the innermost reduction (loaded once per (kd,kh,kw,d) into a small register tile) and hoist the weight load outside the d_out loop — currently fused_kernel reloads w_val for every (ic,kd,kh,kw) and re-walks D inside; restructure to accumulate `acc += w[oc,ic,kd,kh,kw] * Σ_d x[ic,d_valid,h_in,w_in]` with the d-sum done in a tight inner loop and weight reused across BLOCK_HW.
- Try BLOCK_HW=128 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3 (and a sweep over BLOCK_HW∈{64,128,256}, num_warps∈{4,8}) via triton.autotune; the kernel is compute-light per element so larger HW tiles amortize the weight loads better.
- Fold the `torch.flip + permute` into a single index expression inside the kernel (read original ConvTranspose weight directly with `w[ic, oc, KD-1-kd, KH-1-kh, KW-1-kw]`) to drop the eval-time buffer and let the channels-first weight stay coalesced along OC.
large_guidance:
- Recast as an im2col-style GEMM: M=OC, N=BLOCK_HW (output spatial tile per batch), K=IC*KD*KH*KW, with the depth-mean folded as `(1/D) * Σ_{d_out} Σ_{kd valid} x[ic, d_out-1+kd, ...]` precomputed implicitly by an inner d-loop that builds a K-vector of input sums per spatial position; then a single `tl.dot(W_tile, X_tile)` per K-chunk produces the (OC×HW) tile in tensor cores instead of the current scalar outer-product.
- One program per (B, OC-tile, HW-tile); persist the OC-tile of weights in registers/SRAM and stream the K dimension. Apply softmax across OC after the GEMM by doing a second pass within the program (or use a 2-stage kernel: GEMM-with-bias writes a small (OC,HW) tile to shared, then reduce-max/exp/sum/tanh/scale in-place before storing) so we never round-trip through HBM.
- Use channels-last-ish layout for the input slice (load IC contiguously per (d,h,w)) and pre-pad H,W by 1 on the host (or via masked loads with hoisted bounds) to remove the per-kw spatial_valid mask from the hot loop.
